name: IEC logic identity element
summary: Element marked = whose output is active only when all inputs stand at the same logic state.
description: The = qualifier defines a logic identity function: the output is active when every input is in the same state, whether all active or all inactive. For two inputs this is the equivalence or exclusive-NOR function, but with three or more inputs it is a distinct agreement check.

Identity elements are useful for voting and agreement logic, such as confirming that three redundant transmitters agree before allowing an action. The drawing should state what happens on disagreement, since the element only reports whether agreement exists.
The symbol does not provide majority selection. If two-out-of-three voting is intended, a different element or a combination of AND and OR elements is needed.
readingNotes: With three or more inputs, read = as all equal, not as majority.
Check what downstream logic does on a disagreement.
drawingChecklist: Use = only where full agreement is intended.
Label redundant inputs with their channel identifiers.
Show the disagreement response on the same sheet.
distinction: A negated =1 element means not exactly one active; it matches identity only for two inputs.
